office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Eight-year incumbent Beth Doglio, who chairs the House Environment & Energy Committee, faces Republican Don Hewett, an Air Force veteran and engineer running for the first time with no stated policy platform and no reported fundraising.

candidates.summary: Eight-year state representative and chair of the House Environment & Energy Committee, formerly a climate and conservation advocate, running on her record on climate, labor, housing and gun legislation.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, and for the 2025 capital gains and B&O tax bills [S5][S7][S8]
Chairs the House Environment & Energy Committee; cites Clean Buildings standards and sponsors HB 2515 on data centers and other large energy users [S2][S4][S12]
Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the parental-rights law [S6]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council, Washington Conservation Action and the Alliance for Gun Responsibility [S3]

taxes.basis: Yes on ESSB 6346, ESSB 5813 and ESHB 2081, and prime sponsor of an executive-compensation surcharge (HB 1785).

spending.basis: Pledges to 'continue to invest' and protect a strong social safety net and public employees; voted for the 2025-27 operating budget.

housing.basis: Voted for 2025 rent stabilization (EHB 1217), cites added funding to house the vulnerable, endorsed by the Housing Alliance.

climate.basis: Chairs Environment & Energy, led Clean Buildings standards, voted for clean fuels changes, former Climate Solutions advisor.

experience.basis: Eight years in the House and a standing committee chair.

immigration.basis: Voted for 2SHB 2105 (immigrant worker protections) and SSB 5855 (limits on law-enforcement face coverings).

social.basis: Former Pro-Choice Washington political director, endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance and LGBTQ+ Victory Fund, opposes I-638.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 and against Republican amendments to it; opposes I-1.

tech.basis: Prime sponsor of HB 2515 regulating emerging large energy use facilities such as data centers.

candidates.summary: Air Force veteran and engineer running for office for the first time; describes himself as 'not a professional politician' and states no policy platform.
highlights: Former Air Force 96th Bomb Wing police officer and executive engineer [S1]
Pamphlet statement: 'I am not red, I am not blue. I am red, white, and blue.' [S1]
Reports $0 raised and spent with the PDC [S2]

experience.basis: No elected experience; presents himself as a non-politician and regular citizen.
